/-!
# Voronoi diagram: Voronoi's conjecture on parallelohedra

A *parallelohedron* is a convex polytope $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ with nonempty interior whose
translates tile $\mathbb{R}^d$. The *Voronoi diagram* of a lattice $L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$
(in the Euclidean metric) is the tiling of $\mathbb{R}^d$ by the translates $p + V_L$, $p \in L$,
of the Dirichlet–Voronoi cell
$$V_L = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^d : \|x\| \le \|x - p\| \text{ for all } p \in L\}$$
of the origin. Voronoi (1908) conjectured that every parallelohedron is the image of the
Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of some lattice under an affine transformation. Equivalently, for every
parallelohedron $P$ there are an affine transformation $A$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ and a lattice $L$
such that $A$ carries a tiling of $\mathbb{R}^d$ by translates of $P$ (namely the lattice tiling
$\{A^{-1}(p + V_L) : p \in L\}$) onto the Voronoi diagram of $L$.

The conjecture is known to hold for $d \le 5$ and is open for $d \ge 6$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Voronoi diagram*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voronoi_diagram)
- [Wikipedia, *Parallelohedron*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallelohedron)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- G. Voronoi, *Nouvelles applications des paramètres continus à la théorie des formes
  quadratiques. Deuxième mémoire. Recherches sur les paralléloèdres primitifs*,
  J. Reine Angew. Math. 134 (1908), 198–287 and 136 (1909), 67–181.
-/

blocks.docstring:
The translates `t +ᵥ P`, `t ∈ T`, of a set `P ⊆ ℝ^d` form a **tiling** of `ℝ^d` if they
cover `ℝ^d` and have pairwise disjoint interiors.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `tilesByTranslation` in FormalConjecturesForMathlib; `MeasureTheory.IsFundamentalDomain` (group-action/measure formulation, wrong shape for a general translation set T).
justification.name: VoronoiDiagram.IsTilingByTranslates
justification.why_needed: The translates t +ᵥ P (t ∈ T) cover ℝ^d and have pairwise disjoint interiors — the standard notion of a tiling by a closed tile. The repo's `tilesByTranslation` (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Analysis/Fourier/SpectralSets.lean) is measure-theoretic (a.e. cover / null overlaps, countable T) and lives on `Fin d → ℝ` rather than `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`, which the Euclidean Voronoi cell requires; for polytopes with nonempty interior the two notions agree, but the topological one is the standard one for polytope tilings and avoids mixing type synonyms.

blocks.name: IsTilingByTranslates
blocks.text:
/-- The translates `t +ᵥ P`, `t ∈ T`, of a set `P ⊆ ℝ^d` form a **tiling** of `ℝ^d` if they
cover `ℝ^d` and have pairwise disjoint interiors. -/
def IsTilingByTranslates (P T : Set (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  (⋃ t ∈ T, t +ᵥ P) = Set.univ ∧
    T.Pairwise fun t₁ t₂ => Disjoint (interior (t₁ +ᵥ P)) (interior (t₂ +ᵥ P))

blocks.code:
def voronoiCell (S : Set (ℝ^d)) (p : ℝ^d) : Set (ℝ^d) :=
  {x | ∀ q ∈ S, dist x p ≤ dist x q}
blocks.docstring:
The (closed) **Voronoi cell** of the site `p` with respect to a set of sites `S ⊆ ℝ^d`: the
set of points of `ℝ^d` whose Euclidean distance to `p` does not exceed their distance to any site
in `S`. The Voronoi cells `voronoiCell S p`, `p ∈ S`, form the **Voronoi diagram** of `S`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `MeasureTheory.IsFundamentalDomain` and `ZLattice` fundamental-domain API (parallelepiped `ZSpan.fundamentalDomain`), neither of which is the Voronoi cell.
justification.name: VoronoiDiagram.voronoiCell
justification.why_needed: No Voronoi cell / Dirichlet–Voronoi domain exists in Mathlib (only a TODO in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Group/GeometryOfNumbers.lean) or in the repo. Defined as the closed cell {x | ∀ s ∈ S, dist x p ≤ dist x s} in `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`, so the metric is Euclidean as the conjecture requires.

@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem voronoi_diagram :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (d : ℕ) (P T : Set (ℝ^d)), IsConvexPolytope P → (interior P).Nonempty →
      IsTilingByTranslates P T →
        ∃ (A : ℝ^d ≃ᵃ[ℝ] ℝ^d) (L : Submodule ℤ (ℝ^d)) (_ : DiscreteTopology L)
          (_ : IsZLattice ℝ L), A '' P = voronoiCell L 0 := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Voronoi's conjecture.** Does every higher-dimensional tiling by translations of convex polytope
tiles have an affine transformation taking it to a Voronoi diagram?

Precisely: let $d \ge 0$, let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a convex polytope with nonempty
interior, and let $T \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a set of translation vectors such that the
translates $t + P$, $t \in T$, tile $\mathbb{R}^d$ (so $P$ is a *parallelohedron*). Do there exist
an affine bijection $A$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ and a lattice $L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $A(P)$
is the Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of the origin in $L$ for the Euclidean metric? Equivalently, does
some affine transformation $A$ take a tiling of $\mathbb{R}^d$ by translates of $P$ (the lattice
tiling $\{A^{-1}(p + A(P)) : p \in L\}$) to the Voronoi diagram of a lattice $L$?

Here a lattice is a discrete additive subgroup of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that spans $\mathbb{R}^d$. The
hypothesis that $P$ has nonempty interior excludes degenerate lower-dimensional polytopes, whose
translates could otherwise cover $\mathbb{R}^d$ with trivially disjoint (empty) interiors.

The conjecture is known to hold for $d \le 5$ and is open for $d \ge 6$.

claims.decomposer_note: This is Voronoi's conjecture on parallelohedra: for every dimension d and every (bounded, full-dimensional) convex polytope P whose translates tile Euclidean R^d, there exist an affine bijection A of R^d and a lattice L such that A maps the tiling onto the Voronoi tessellation of L (i.e. A(P) is the Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of L); 'Voronoi diagram' here means the diagram of a point lattice in the Euclidean metric (any translational tiling by a convex polytope is automatically a lattice tiling), 'higher-dimensional' means all d (known true for d ≤ 5, open for d ≥ 6), and degenerate tiles (empty interior or unbounded) must be excluded by hypothesis.
claims.reviewer_why: c01's declaration (universal quantification over the tiling's translation set T, EuclideanSpace via ℝ^d notation, affine bijection, full-rank discrete Z-lattice via DiscreteTopology + IsZLattice, closed Euclidean Voronoi cell of the origin) is faithful; final file uses it with definitions/docstrings/test lemmas merged from c03 and c05 (equivalent content). c02, c03, c05, c06 are equally faithful (∃ T vs ∀ T is immaterial since T is absent from the conclusion). c04, c07, c08 rejected: they use `Fin d → ℝ`, whose Mathlib metric is the sup-norm, so their 'Voronoi cell' is an L∞ cell rather than the Euclidean Dirichlet–Voronoi cell — a different conjecture.

context:
In mathematics, a Voronoi diagram is a partition of a plane into regions close to each of a given set of objects. It can be classified also as a tessellation. In the simplest case, these objects are just finitely many points in the plane (called seeds, sites, or generators). For each seed there is a corresponding region, called a Voronoi cell comprising all points of the plane closer to that seed than to any other. The Voronoi diagram of a set of points is dual to that set's Delaunay triangulation.
The Voronoi diagram is named after mathematician Georgy Voronoy, and is also called a Voronoi tessellation, a Voronoi decomposition, a Voronoi partition, or a Dirichlet tessellation (after Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet). Voronoi cells are also known as Thiessen polygons, after Alfred H. Thiessen. Voronoi diagrams have practical and theoretical applications in many fields, mainly in science and technology, but also in visual art.

decomposition_objections.text: The note's justification "any translational tiling by a convex polytope is automatically a lattice tiling" is inaccurate: every parallelohedron admits a face-to-face lattice tiling (Venkov/McMullen), but a given translational tiling need not be a lattice tiling (e.g. rows of squares shifted by irrational amounts). Consequently the note's primary phrasing "A maps the tiling onto the Voronoi tessellation of L" cannot be formalized with the given tiling T (it would be false in ℝ², turning the open conjecture into a disproved statement). I followed the note's parenthetical formulation "A(P) is the Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of L", which is the standard statement of Voronoi's conjecture and is equivalent to A mapping the lattice tiling by P onto the Voronoi diagram of L. Otherwise the table (one slot, lattice Voronoi diagram, Euclidean metric, all d, bounded full-dimensional tile) is correct.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Voronoi diagram: Voronoi's conjecture on parallelohedra

A *parallelohedron* is a convex polytope $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ with nonempty interior whose
translates tile $\mathbb{R}^d$. The *Voronoi diagram* of a lattice $L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$
(in the Euclidean metric) is the tiling of $\mathbb{R}^d$ by the translates $p + V_L$, $p \in L$,

$$V_L = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^d : \|x\| \le \|x - p\| \text{ for all } p \in L\}$$
of the origin. Voronoi (1908) conjectured that every parallelohedron is the image of the
Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of some lattice under an affine transformation. Equivalently, for every
parallelohedron $P$ there are an affine transformation $A$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ and a lattice $L$
such that $A$ carries a tiling of $\mathbb{R}^d$ by translates of $P$ (namely the lattice tiling
$\{A^{-1}(p + V_L) : p \in L\}$) onto the Voronoi diagram of $L$.

The conjecture is known to hold for $d \le 5$ and is open for $d \ge 6$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Voronoi diagram*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voronoi_diagram)
- [Wikipedia, *Parallelohedron*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallelohedron)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- G. Voronoi, *Nouvelles applications des paramètres continus à la théorie des formes
  quadratiques. Deuxième mémoire. Recherches sur les paralléloèdres primitifs*,
  J. Reine Angew. Math. 134 (1908), 198–287 and 136 (1909), 67–181.
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry Pointwise

namespace VoronoiDiagram

variable {d : ℕ}

/-- A subset `P` of `ℝ^d` is a **convex polytope** if it is the convex hull of a finite set of
points. Such a set is automatically compact and convex. -/
def IsConvexPolytope (P : Set (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∃ s : Finset (ℝ^d), P = convexHull ℝ (s : Set (ℝ^d))

/-- The translates `t +ᵥ P`, `t ∈ T`, of a set `P ⊆ ℝ^d` form a **tiling** of `ℝ^d` if they
cover `ℝ^d` and have pairwise disjoint interiors. -/
def IsTilingByTranslates (P T : Set (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  (⋃ t ∈ T, t +ᵥ P) = Set.univ ∧
    T.Pairwise fun t₁ t₂ => Disjoint (interior (t₁ +ᵥ P)) (interior (t₂ +ᵥ P))

/-- The (closed) **Voronoi cell** of the site `p` with respect to a set of sites `S ⊆ ℝ^d`: the
set of points of `ℝ^d` whose Euclidean distance to `p` does not exceed their distance to any site
in `S`. The Voronoi cells `voronoiCell S p`, `p ∈ S`, form the **Voronoi diagram** of `S`. -/
def voronoiCell (S : Set (ℝ^d)) (p : ℝ^d) : Set (ℝ^d) :=
  {x | ∀ q ∈ S, dist x p ≤ dist x q}

/-- The convex hull of a finite set of points is a convex polytope. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem isConvexPolytope_convexHull (s : Finset (ℝ^d)) :
    IsConvexPolytope (convexHull ℝ (s : Set (ℝ^d))) :=
  ⟨s, rfl⟩

/-- The whole space is tiled by its single translate by `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem isTilingByTranslates_univ_singleton :
    IsTilingByTranslates (Set.univ : Set (ℝ^d)) {0} := by
  simp [IsTilingByTranslates]

/-- A site belongs to its own Voronoi cell. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem mem_voronoiCell_self (S : Set (ℝ^d)) (p : ℝ^d) : p ∈ voronoiCell S p :=
  fun _ _ => by simp

/-- The Voronoi cell of a single site is the whole space. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem voronoiCell_singleton (p : ℝ^d) : voronoiCell {p} p = Set.univ := by
  simp [voronoiCell]

/--
**Voronoi's conjecture.** Does every higher-dimensional tiling by translations of convex polytope
tiles have an affine transformation taking it to a Voronoi diagram?

Precisely: let $d \ge 0$, let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a convex polytope with nonempty
interior, and let $T \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a set of translation vectors such that the
translates $t + P$, $t \in T$, tile $\mathbb{R}^d$ (so $P$ is a *parallelohedron*). Do there exist
an affine bijection $A$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ and a lattice $L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $A(P)$
is the Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of the origin in $L$ for the Euclidean metric? Equivalently, does
some affine transformation $A$ take a tiling of $\mathbb{R}^d$ by translates of $P$ (the lattice
tiling $\{A^{-1}(p + A(P)) : p \in L\}$) to the Voronoi diagram of a lattice $L$?

Here a lattice is a discrete additive subgroup of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that spans $\mathbb{R}^d$. The
hypothesis that $P$ has nonempty interior excludes degenerate lower-dimensional polytopes, whose
translates could otherwise cover $\mathbb{R}^d$ with trivially disjoint (empty) interiors.

The conjecture is known to hold for $d \le 5$ and is open for $d \ge 6$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem voronoi_diagram :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (d : ℕ) (P T : Set (ℝ^d)), IsConvexPolytope P → (interior P).Nonempty →
      IsTilingByTranslates P T →
        ∃ (A : ℝ^d ≃ᵃ[ℝ] ℝ^d) (L : Submodule ℤ (ℝ^d)) (_ : DiscreteTopology L)
          (_ : IsZLattice ℝ L), A '' P = voronoiCell L 0 := by
  sorry

end VoronoiDiagram

items: The Wikipedia list entry is terse; the article (Voronoi diagram) only gives the definition of Voronoi cells. The precise conjecture was taken from the standard literature formulation (Voronoi 1908; Wikipedia 'Parallelohedron'): every parallelohedron (convex polytope whose translates tile ℝ^d) is affinely equivalent to the Dirichlet–Voronoi polytope of a lattice. Formalized as: for every such P (and every tiling T by its translates), ∃ affine bijection A and lattice L with A(P) = Voronoi cell of 0 in L. Composing A with a translation makes 'cell of the origin' WLOG.

The conclusion is about the tile P rather than literally about the given tiling T. Reason: the literal reading 'A maps the given tiling onto a Voronoi diagram' is false already in ℝ² — rows of unit squares shifted by non-integer offsets form a translational tiling that is not face-to-face, whereas every Voronoi diagram is face-to-face and affine maps preserve face-to-face-ness. The conjecture is about P (equivalently, about its face-to-face lattice tiling), which is what the file states; the docstring records the equivalent 'A maps the lattice tiling {P + t : t ∈ Λ} onto the Voronoi diagram of L' reading.

'Higher-dimensional' was read as 'for all d : ℕ'. The statement for d = 0 is trivially true and for d ≤ 5 is a theorem; the quantification over all d is exactly the open conjecture (open for d ≥ 6). The `answer(sorry) ↔ …` form is used because the source is phrased as a question; `answer(True)` = the conjecture holds.
'Lattice' is formalized as `L : Submodule ℤ (ℝ^d)` with `DiscreteTopology L` and `IsZLattice ℝ L` (full rank). Full rank is essential: the Voronoi cell of a lower-rank discrete subgroup is unbounded.

Ambient space is `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)` (notation `ℝ^d`) so that `dist` in `voronoiCell` is the Euclidean metric, as required for Voronoi diagrams of lattices. The Voronoi cell is the closed cell (≤), matching the closed polytope P.

Tiling requires cover of `Set.univ` by the closed translates and pairwise disjoint interiors; countability of T is automatic (disjoint nonempty open sets in ℝ^d). Hypothesis `(interior P).Nonempty` excludes degenerate tiles (e.g. a segment in ℝ²), whose translates satisfy the tiling condition vacuously and for which the conclusion fails.

reviewer_notes: Reading: the list entry is terse. All candidates and the decomposition notes agree the intended problem is Voronoi's conjecture on parallelohedra: every bounded full-dimensional convex polytope tiling R^d by translations is an affine image of the Euclidean Voronoi cell of a full-rank lattice. The literal reading 'the given tiling is mapped onto a Voronoi diagram' is false in R^2 (brick-wall tilings by squares are translational, even lattice, tilings but not face-to-face; Voronoi diagrams are face-to-face and affine maps preserve this), so it cannot be the open problem; the final docstring records the equivalent tiling-level formulation via the lattice tiling A^{-1}(p + A(P)). Candidates' objection to the notes' claim 'any translational tiling by a convex polytope is automatically a lattice tiling' is correct (only: every parallelohedron ADMITS a lattice face-to-face tiling, Venkov/McMullen); this does not affect the formalized content. Modeling: convex polytope = convex hull of a Finset (bounded, closed); (interior P).Nonempty excludes degenerate lower-dimensional tiles (which would vacuously tile and make the answer trivially No); tiling = translates cover univ with pairwise disjoint interiors (standard for closed tiles; countability/local finiteness automatic for full-dimensional compact tiles); lattice = Submodule ℤ with DiscreteTopology and IsZLattice ℝ (span_top); closed cell with ≤ matches closed P; 'higher-dimensional' read as all d : ℕ (d = 0, 1 trivially true; known for d ≤ 5, open d ≥ 6). answer(True) = positive answer. Compiled with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning. c02's extra research-solved variant for d ≤ 5 was not included as it is outside the slot table. c04/c07/c08 rejected for using the sup-norm metric on Fin d → ℝ (verified via dist_pi_def).
